fixes.explanation: Elihu, the young man now speaking to Job, says it plainly: “My words are from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what I know.” He puts that on the table before he gets into his speech. It's his own claim about himself, so keep listening to see what he does with it.

Elihu, the young man speaking to Job, doesn't point to his elders here. He says, “My words are from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what I know.” So he's pointing to his own heart and what he knows.

You've got the right body part, friend, but a different adjective. Elihu, the young man speaking to Job, says, “My words are from an upright heart…” He's calling his heart upright, not troubled. A troubled heart sounds more like where Job has been living lately.

That's right. Elihu tells Job, “Surely no fear of me should terrify you; nor will my hand be heavy upon you.” He's telling Job there's no need to be afraid of him. He's saying he won't come down hard on him.
Elihu quotes Job saying, “Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.” Those are heavy words, friend, and Elihu repeats them right back to him. Elihu is about to answer them.

I get why you'd reach for friend, because that's what you'd hope God would be called. But in the quote, Job says, “Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.” Enemy is the word in the very words Elihu says he heard from Job (Job 33:8). Elihu is about to say Job isn't right in this matter (Job 33:12).
Elihu asks, “Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?” He's questioning the complaint itself. He's about to say God does speak, in one way and another (Job 33:14).

Elihu says God speaks “In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men as they slumber on their beds…” So here the night is when God speaks. People are asleep, and that's when He opens their ears (Job 33:16).

A trumpet would certainly wake the neighborhood, friend. But Elihu doesn't mention one here. He says God speaks “In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men…” It's a dream or vision while people sleep.
Elihu doesn't say anything about testing here. He says, “But if you have something to say, answer me; speak up, for I would like to vindicate you.” To vindicate is to clear someone's name.
